boundaries: Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.
completion_conditions: All required act objectives have reached their authored endings. An early departure can end play honestly, but does not count as completion of unplayed acts.

The escort has reached the clinic destination with the surviving people and cargo, or the failed journey has ended at a stated safe retreat location with the observed losses and last known locations reported. An ongoing journey is unfinished.

Closing event: the clinic or receiving Guild contact accounts for Dev, Oss and the other actual travellers, receives the medicine or loss report, settles the earned 40 gp recovery and conditional 20 gp medicine payment or agreed partial fee, and responds to the crew's immediate shelter and care needs. Record the wagon loss and surviving bargain with Keth without adding another compulsory trip.
continuation_conditions: Further adventures require the player’s interest after this story has a complete ending. Surviving contacts and obligations can carry forward.

outcomes.outcome: This adventure has reached its authored closing event with the actual successes or losses acknowledged. Its earned result and continuing consequences remain true.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.
gm_guidance.railroading: Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

facts.fact: A Guild supply caravan is overdue on the Verdant Margin route. Fresh wheel ruts end where new growth covers an old fork.
The Guild offers 40 gp for the people’s recovery and 20 gp more for the urgently needed medicine. Food, rope and a route sketch are available on agreed loan.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

completion_conditions: The party reaches the wayhouse and establishes Dev's and Oss's positions and the medicine's location. The crew is freed beyond Keth's control or an ended rescue attempt records who remains captive, escaped or lost; account for Ina's known escape separately.
The party has exited the immediate wayhouse danger with the actual surviving people and carried cargo. Record Oss's condition, the medicine and marker kit rather than assuming recovery.

Closing event: on safe ground the player and available crew choose the low-road, ridge or withdrawal route based on the ledger and the rescued people's needs, and state whom and what they are taking. Choosing withdrawal does not complete the unplayed escort; play that journey or end early with the rescue report.

opening_direction: Start at a Guild roadside post overlooking the caravan’s last known trail. A courier shows the missed arrival entry, broken harness and map. Offer the rescue contract without assigning the player an earlier connection to the missing people.
premise: Track a missing caravan into the Verdant Margin, break it out of a raider-held wayhouse and escort the survivors through a forest that has swallowed the road.

secrets.fact: Dev shared some food with stranded travellers before Keth seized the rest; his ledger and the travellers distinguish aid from theft.

reveal.condition: Inspect the ledger or speak with the rescued travellers.

branches: Approach by drain, negotiate from the yard or fight for the hall.
Recover the people first and bargain for the medicine later if health or supplies make that necessary.
consequences: Record surviving enemies, medicine crates, food actually left, Oss’s condition and the marker kit.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

planned_encounters: Fight 1, loading-yard lookout. Rift-raider outrider (humanoid): AC 12, HP 10, speed 30 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 slashing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. Can instead shoot a shortbow at +3, range 80/320 ft, for 1d6+1 piercing. This lightly armed scout has no innate spells or psychic damage. Uses half cover behind the wall and spends an action signalling C if able. It retreats into C at 3 HP. For the solo baseline this is the same surviving actor later, not an extra fresh foe.

Fight 2, Keth in the main hall. Keth (humanoid): AC 13, HP 17, speed 30 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+2 slashing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  Keth prioritises escape with the medicine; fire is not used around the captives. The lookout, if present, carries goods rather than adding attacks against a lone baseline character. Keth yields at 5 HP if offered safety. For solo level 1 use HP 11, damage 1d4+1, and keep the lookout outside C.
situations: Cast and truth. Driver Dev turned toward an old stone wayhouse when roots broke the axle. He shared food with stranded travellers; the missing cargo is not all stolen. Raider leader Keth then seized the wayhouse, demanding medicine and wagon iron. Scout Ina escaped through a drainage channel and left three tied reed markers. Dev protects injured porter Oss, while the raiders want saleable goods and a safe retreat. Their cause is local scarcity and predation, not a secret world-spanning cult.

Tracking leg. The torn harness and visible ruts give a reliable route to the fork. Wisdom (Survival) DC 12 reads Ina’s reeds and finds the drain approach, saving a dangerous detour. Failure still reaches the wayhouse by the high trail, but the lookout sees the approach unless Dexterity (Stealth) DC 12 succeeds. A player who moves openly gets challenged rather than automatically shot. An overgrown gully can be crossed by a properly anchored rope without a roll; rushing through the thorn curtain requires Dexterity save DC 12, taking 1d4 piercing on failure and none on success. A supported spell or deliberate cutting supplies other approaches with stated time/resource costs.

Wayhouse layout. A outer loading yard holds the damaged wagon behind a low wall. B stable connects to A and C, the occupied main hall. D loft overlooks C by a broken stair. E dry cellar connects C to Ina’s drain outside the wall. The medicine is in C; Dev and Oss shelter in B. A loose stone niche in E holds the old route marker kit, useful in Act 2. The drain permits Small or unarmoured crawling access as the fiction supports; do not invent a class restriction. Removing bulky gear creates a real carried-equipment decision.

Rescue and control. A lookout guards A. Keth waits in C with the medicine and a crossbar holding B’s door shut. A quiet Dexterity check with thieves’ tools DC 12 releases B from the drain side; failure scrapes metal and alerts Keth, but the door still has an exposed bar accessible through C. A Strength (Athletics) DC 13 lift can shift the fallen beam inside B off Oss; a lever and two helpers make the lift safe without rolling. Medicine DC 10 determines whether Oss can walk with support; failure means transport on a stretcher until properly assessed, not immediate death. Actual healing can restore HP but does not silently straighten a broken axle.

Negotiation and treasure. Keth accepts iron fittings worth 10 gp and a witnessed withdrawal if the party can show the drain makes his position untenable; Persuasion DC 13 may reduce that demand, not create consent to every order. Force is a prepared alternative. The marker kit and Dev’s ledger explain a ridge route, and 15 gp in recovered Guild coin belongs to the caravan. The party keeps its contract payment, not every merchant’s goods. Once the raiders withdraw or are defeated, the cellar can support a secure short rest.

structure.title: Where the wheels stopped

branches: Use the slow secure ridge, the short difficult culvert or a feasible supported magical route.
Abandon replaceable cargo to protect people, or spend time and equipment to recover both.
consequences: Earlier rescue decisions determine helpers, medicines, food and information; never reset them for this act.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

planned_encounters: Fight 3, two hungry young Rifthounds at the culvert or ridge camp, never both. Young Rifthound (monstrosity): AC 12, HP 11, speed 40 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 piercing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. No phase-step, regeneration or pack bonus. It withdraws at 3 HP if food or an escape remains. One initially drags spilled food while the other engages; a second attacker is appropriate only if the actual party can bear it. Use the rocks for cover and narrow approach. Solo level 1: one active hound, HP 8, bite 1d4+1, the second already feeding off-screen. Food diversion and a supported animal-related ability can avoid the fight.
situations: Two real routes. The low road is half a day shorter but its bridge has been engulfed by roots; a dark culvert below remains passable on foot. The ridge road is longer, with a narrow stone traverse and a sheltered camp. Dev prefers the ridge for Oss if enough food remains. The rescued marker kit reveals sound anchor holes on that traverse; without it, finding them requires Investigation DC 12, with failure costing daylight and a return to the obvious main trail rather than dropping the party into a void.

Escort resources. Count the party’s and caravan’s actual rations, load and light. The crew can haul a litter if protected; ordinary labour is not extra combat actions. An agreed overnight camp on the ridge permits a long rest if the normal requirements are met, at the cost of a later medicine arrival. Say what delay means before it is chosen: the destination clinic can ration existing stock for a day, then postpones routine care. There is no invented instant-death patient timer. Magical food, shelter, healing or movement count only when the selected character has and spends the relevant ability.

The swallowed bridge. Roots cover intact stones and a ten-foot gap. A rope traverse with a secured belay is slow and safe; an unsupported jump uses the actual jump rules, with Athletics DC 12 only for the slippery landing when uncertain. Failure catches the lower ledge for 1d6 bludgeoning, leaving a visible rope-rescue route. In the culvert, carried packs scrape loudly and attract the hungry hound encounter unless the party lays out spare food or succeeds on a Stealth DC 12 approach. Failure causes the encounter from a known entrance; it does not remove the exit.

Ridge alternative and pursuit. On the ridge the same hounds feed near the sheltered camp, so locating them through Perception DC 12 lets the party choose a wide detour or prepare a defensible position. Choosing this route does not add a second pack. Keth only pursues if alive, unwilling to accept the outcome and equipped to follow; a concluded bargain removes that threat. Use the surviving raider’s existing wounds. A driver’s decoy load or an honest settlement can finish pursuit; never respawn raiders solely to produce another fight.

Arrival and reward. Deliver the people and whatever cargo survived. Pay 40 gp for their recovery and the additional 20 gp if the agreed medicine reaches the clinic; Dev can negotiate a proportionate fee after an honest partial recovery. The clinic returns borrowed gear and can provide normal care, not unearned full restoration. Resolve the saved travellers’ thanks, the damage to the Guild wagon and any bargain with Keth. End at the route’s destination; the caravan is not secretly carrying a key to the Anchor Doors.

title: The Long Way Round
tone: A wilderness rescue followed by a hard-fought escort.
unsupported_mechanics: Site phasing, enemy motives, alarms and engineering objectives are explicitly described GM adjudications. Checks, saves, damage, spells, rest and admitted combat use the D&D Ruleset. No extra automatic hazard, pursuit, faction, economy or crafting subsystem is installed.
Listed creature profiles are weaker or specialised Setting adaptations with declared statistics. They do not assert support for unencoded powers from the original monster entries.

Gold and salvage become awarded possessions only when recorded through the applicable inventory/state path. SRD Lite has a reduced spell list (117 supported spells) and no consumables; consumables belong to future SRD Full. A narrative reward never installs a magic-item feature, restores a slot or applies healing.
